hook: "Created these Weekender Bag ad concepts after studying what's working for leading DTC travel brands on Meta."
idea: Four ad concepts, four conversion angles (problem-solution, lifestyle, benefits, social proof) — one angle per creative, because good ads don't try to say everything.
sequencing: Hook: concepts from studying winning DTC travel brands.
The rule: good ads don't say everything.
formatting: Portfolio post: the research note → the 4-angle structure → the one-idea rule. Photo.
why_it_works: 'Studying what's working' borrows the winners' authority. The one-idea rule is the discipline most advertisers lack — naming it is the value.
what_to_steal: The one-angle-per-creative rule for LC: each dupe carries exactly one conversion angle — problem-solution gets its own cut, never mixed with lifestyle. The 4-angle set is LC's creative matrix.

hook: "the 5 ad creative formats that convert highest in dropshipping right now ranked by performance:"
body: The ranked 5: (1) UGC problem/solution — real/AI person describes the problem, shows product, shows result; 30-45s, phone feel; 'I was waking up every night with back pain… first night I slept through'; converts highest, looks like a friend. (2) 'TikTok made me buy it' — fast cuts, trending audio, <15s demo; impulse <$40. (3) Us vs them split — 15-20s, visual conflict, highest CTR. (4) Founder talking head — 'I designed this because I was tired of [problem]'; retargets 2-3x, face = familiarity. (5) Text-overlay slideshow — 5-7 images, 'problem → solution → proof → offer'; 70-80% of video performance at 5% effort. Common thread: native, not ads — the moment it looks produced, the brain scrolls.
cta: none explicit — the ranking is the content.
idea: UGC problem/solution ranks #1 in dropshipping: problem → product → result in 30-45s with a phone-recorded feel — it converts highest because it looks like a friend recommending, not an ad.
sequencing: #1: UGC problem/solution — the structure + example line.
The common thread: native, not produced.
The rule: best ad doesn't look like an ad.
formatting: Ranked playbook: 5 formats with runtime, mechanics, and example lines; the common-thread close.
why_it_works: Ranking by performance (not opinion) + a concrete example line per format makes it immediately usable. 'Looks like a friend, not an ad' is the whole UGC thesis in one line.
what_to_steal: The #1 format as LC's workhorse: 'I was [tarnish problem]… my friend told me about this… first [result]' — 30-45s, phone feel, problem → product → result. The slideshow stat (70-80% of video at 5% effort) justifies LC's slideshow lane economics.
